summary: Clarify interaction between per-route concurrency limits and account-wide token/quota caps causing 429s
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses during sustained production traffic after they reduced their per-route concurrency limits to enforce fair usage across multiple apps. They expect account-wide token quotas to be consumed independently from per-route concurrency throttles, but observed request-level 429s that appear correlated with the global token cap being reached. Impact: Multiple downstream pipelines are failing mid-run and retrying backoff loops, increasing latency and cost. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod/us-west-2, multiple API keys in a single tenant, load pattern is ~120 concurrent streams across 8 routes with long-tail token usage. Request: Clarify exact precedence and interactions between per-route concurrency settings and account-wide token/quota limits, and whether per-route limits can be configured to avoid triggering account-level 429s during bursty long-sequence requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer created 8 API routes under the same tenant and set per-route concurrency to 20 each
2) Launched steady load of short requests from 40 workers + occasional long-sequence generation from 10 workers
3) Observed many 429 responses originating from the API gateway; timing aligns with when long-sequence jobs hit token quota thresholds
4) They temporarily increased account token limit and 429 rates dropped, but per-route queues then grew and latency spiked
5) Reverted token limit and reduced per-route concurrency; 429s returned unexpectedly for short requests as long jobs continued

investigation_notes: Support initial triage: 429s present for both short and long requests; logs indicate 'account_quota_exhausted' and decisions from rate-limiter referencing both per-route and tenant windows.
Hypothesis A: account-wide token quota is being consumed by long-sequence jobs causing early 429s for other routes even when their per-route concurrency is below limit.
Hypothesis B: per-route concurrency enforcement queues requests but account-level token accounting is evaluated at acceptance time leading to unexpected rejections when token budget is low.
Observed correlation between spikes in avg_seq_len and immediate jump in 429s across routes — supports Hypothesis A.

Checked dedicated pool settings: tenant_token_budget set to 1.2M tokens/min, per-route concurrency windows active. Customer was running 3 long jobs averaging 20k tokens each which can exhaust minute budget quickly.
Ran local simulation with similar traffic pattern; reproduced 429s when long-sequence token consumption crosses tenant_token_budget even though per-route concurrency remains within configured limits.
Shared sample logs and spike graphs with SRE via #support and linked infra PRs for rate-limiter heuristics (infra/rate-limiter#412).
customer_communication: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Customer (Bluewave): 'We reduced per-route concurrency to be polite to other teams, but short requests still fail with 429s. Why are short requests impacted if their route has free concurrency slots?'

2026-03-05 10:03 - Support (Aisha): 'We are investigating; initial evidence suggests long-sequence token consumption at the tenant level is exhausting the account token budget which causes account-level throttles. We're reproducing with a simulator and will confirm precedence rules and mitigation options.'

2026-03-06 14:28 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): 'Confirmed reproduction. Rate limiter enforces tenant token budget at acceptance time. Per-route concurrency only controls parallel in-flight requests — it does not reserve token budget. Long sequences can therefore cause global 429s even when some routes have concurrency headroom.'

2026-03-07 08:45 - Support (Aisha): 'Temporary mitigation options: increase tenant token budget, limit max sequence length per route, or configure prioritized routing for latency-critical short routes to a separate tenant or dedicated route with isolated quota.'

2026-03-07 12:10 - Customer (Bluewave): 'We'll try splitting latency-sensitive traffic to a separate route and apply sequence-length caps. Please advise recommended thresholds for sequence caps given our workload.'
recommended_actions: 1) Document behavior: account/tenant token quota is evaluated at request acceptance; per-route concurrency does not reserve token budget — long sequences can deplete tenant quota and produce account-level 429s.

2) Recommend configuration: create a separate tenant or dedicated route for latency-sensitive short requests and give it an isolated token budget, or increase tenant_token_budget to accommodate peak long-job consumption.
3) Suggest application-level mitigations: enforce max_tokens on long-running jobs, add client-side token estimation and cost-aware scheduling, and apply exponential backoff for retries.

4) Engineering follow-up: consider adding optional routing/priority weight that can reserve a small guaranteed token slice per route to protect critical short-request paths (tracked as INT-4221 roadmap item).
resolution: Pending customer decision on mitigation. Support provided configuration guidance and temporary workarounds (split traffic, apply max_tokens). Engineering will evaluate a feature to reserve small guaranteed token budgets per route; tracked internally.
